artificial intelligence:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is the broad field of computer science focused on building systems that simulate human intelligence — reasoning, learning, planning, perception.

Key branches: Machine Learning, Deep Learning, NLP, Computer Vision, Robotics.

Real-world: Siri, self-driving cars (Tesla), ChatGPT, Midjourney.
machine learning:
Machine Learning (ML) trains systems to learn patterns from data automatically.

Three main types: Supervised (labeled data), Unsupervised (unlabeled), Reinforcement (reward-based).

Real-world: Netflix recommendations, email spam detection, fraud detection.
deep learning:
Deep Learning uses neural networks with many layers to learn from large datasets.

Why powerful: extracts features from raw data without manual engineering.

Real-world: Face recognition, voice assistants, medical imaging.
neural networks:
Neural Networks are computing systems inspired by the brain — layers of connected nodes.

Structure: Input layer → Hidden layers → Output layer.

Real-world: Google Translate, image recognition, chatbots.
supervised learning:
Supervised Learning trains on labeled data — every input has a known correct output.

Real-world: Email spam filter, house price prediction, medical diagnosis.
unsupervised learning:
Unsupervised Learning finds patterns in data without labels.

Techniques: Clustering, Dimensionality reduction, Anomaly detection.

Real-world: Customer segmentation, news article grouping, fraud detection.
reinforcement learning:
Reinforcement Learning trains an agent via rewards and penalties.

Key concepts: Agent, Environment, Reward, Policy.

Real-world: AlphaGo, game-playing AIs, robot manipulation.
natural language processing:
NLP enables machines to understand and generate human language.

Key tasks: Sentiment analysis, Translation, Summarization, NER.

Real-world: ChatGPT, Claude, Google Translate, Gmail smart compose.
computer vision:
Computer Vision gives machines the ability to interpret images and video.

Key tasks: Object detection, Classification, Facial recognition, Segmentation.

Real-world: Self-driving cars, face unlock, factory quality inspection.
generative ai:
Generative AI creates new content — text, images, audio, video, code.

Key models: GPT-4, Claude (text) | Midjourney, DALL-E (image) | Sora (video).

Real-world: Writing assistants, AI art, code generation.
large language model:
LLMs are deep learning models trained on massive text to understand and generate language.

Famous LLMs: GPT-4 (OpenAI), Claude (Anthropic), Gemini (Google), LLaMA (Meta).

Uses: Chatbots, code generation, document summarization.
random forest:
Random Forest builds many decision trees and combines their predictions.

Why it works: Many weak trees vote together → one strong prediction.

Real-world: Fraud detection, disease risk, stock prediction.
support vector machine:
SVMs find the optimal hyperplane that best separates classes in data.

Kernel trick: handles non-linear data by mapping to higher dimensions.

Real-world: Handwriting recognition, image classification, cancer detection.
transformer:
Transformers are the architecture behind modern LLMs — uses attention mechanisms.

Key innovation: Self-attention allows the model to weigh importance of each word relative to others.

Real-world: GPT, BERT, Claude, T5, Whisper (speech), Vision Transformer.
python:
Python is the dominant language for AI, data science, and automation.

Key libraries: NumPy/Pandas (data), TensorFlow/PyTorch (deep learning), Flask/FastAPI (web).

Used by: Google, NASA, Instagram, Netflix.
javascript:
JavaScript is the primary web language — runs in browsers and on servers (Node.js).

Frameworks: React, Vue, Angular (frontend) | Node.js, Express (backend).

Used by: Facebook, Twitter, Netflix, Airbnb.
flask:
Flask is a lightweight Python web framework for building APIs and web apps.

Key concepts: Routes, Blueprints, Jinja2 templates, SQLAlchemy ORM, SSE streaming.

Used for: REST APIs, microservices, internal tools, ML model serving.
blockchain:
Blockchain is a distributed, immutable ledger across a network of computers.

How it works: Transactions → Blocks → Linked chain → Consensus validation.

Real-world: Bitcoin/Ethereum, smart contracts, supply chain.
cloud computing:
Cloud Computing delivers computing resources over the internet on pay-as-you-go.

Models: IaaS (infrastructure), PaaS (platform), SaaS (software).

Providers: AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure.
cybersecurity:
Cybersecurity protects systems, networks, and data from digital attacks.

Domains: Network security, App security, Cryptography, Incident response.

Threats: Malware, Phishing, Ransomware, DDoS | Tools: Firewalls, MFA, VPNs.
api:
An API lets different software applications communicate with each other.

Types: REST (HTTP), GraphQL (flexible queries), WebSocket (real-time).

Real-world: Weather apps, Login with Google, Stripe payments.
database:
A database stores and manages structured data electronically.

SQL (relational): MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite | NoSQL: MongoDB, Redis.

Uses: User accounts, product catalogs, banking records.
docker:
Docker packages applications and their dependencies into containers.

Why useful: Consistent environment across dev/test/production. 'It works on my machine' solved.

Key concepts: Image, Container, Dockerfile, Docker Compose, Registry.
git:
Git is the most widely used distributed version control system.

Key commands: init, clone, add, commit, push, pull, branch, merge, rebase.

Platforms: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket.
internet of things:
IoT connects physical devices with sensors and internet connectivity.

Examples: Smart home (Alexa, Nest), Wearables (Apple Watch), Industrial sensors.

Challenge: Security and privacy of billions of connected devices.
augmented reality:
AR overlays digital content onto the real world through a screen or camera.

vs VR: AR enhances reality; VR replaces it entirely.

Real-world: Snapchat filters, IKEA Place, Pokemon GO, Surgical navigation.
quantum computing:
Quantum computers use qubits (superposition + entanglement) instead of classical bits.

Advantage: Can solve certain problems exponentially faster than classical computers.

Use cases: Cryptography breaking, drug discovery, optimization problems.

Players: IBM Quantum, Google Sycamore, IonQ, D-Wave.
robotics:
Robotics combines mechanical engineering, electronics, and software for physical task automation.

Key fields: Industrial automation, surgical robots, autonomous vehicles, humanoid robots.

Leading platforms: ROS (Robot Operating System), Boston Dynamics, Tesla Optimus.
edge computing:
Edge Computing processes data near where it's generated — not in a central cloud.

Why it matters: Lower latency, offline operation, reduced bandwidth.

Use cases: Autonomous vehicles, smart factories, rural IoT deployments.
data science:
Data Science extracts insights from structured and unstructured data.

Workflow: Collect → Clean → Analyze → Model → Communicate.

Tools: Python, R, SQL, Jupyter, Tableau | Used in: Healthcare, finance, sports.
rag:
RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) enhances LLMs by retrieving relevant documents before generating.

How it works: Query → Retrieve from vector DB → Inject into prompt → Generate grounded answer.

Why it matters: Reduces hallucination, enables up-to-date answers without retraining.

Tools: LangChain, LlamaIndex, ChromaDB, Pinecone, FAISS.
vector database:
Vector databases store and search high-dimensional embeddings efficiently.

Core operation: Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) search on vectors.

Popular options: ChromaDB (local), Pinecone (cloud), Weaviate, Qdrant, FAISS.
precision agriculture:
Precision agriculture uses technology to optimize crop yield with minimal inputs.

Tools: GPS, drones, soil sensors, satellite imagery, AI yield prediction.

Benefits: Reduces water, fertilizer, and pesticide waste while increasing productivity.

In India: ISRO's Bhuvan, AgriStack, Khethari platform.
agritech:
AgriTech applies technology to improve agriculture productivity and farmer income.

Segments: IoT soil sensors, drone surveillance, AI disease detection, market price apps.

Key Indian players: DeHaat, AgroStar, Fasal, Ninjacart, Khethari.

Opportunity: 60% of India's workforce in agriculture — massive underserved market.
soil science:
Soil Science studies soil composition, structure, and health for agricultural productivity.

Key parameters: pH, NPK (nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium), organic matter, moisture.

In India: ICAR soil health cards help farmers understand their soil type.
crop protection:
Crop protection prevents yield loss from pests, diseases, and weeds.

Methods: Chemical pesticides, biological control, IPM (Integrated Pest Management).

AI application: Disease detection from leaf images using computer vision.
startup:
A startup is a company in its early stages, typically with high growth potential and uncertainty.

Key stages: Idea → MVP → Product-Market Fit → Growth → Scale.

India startup ecosystem: Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai hubs. DPIIT-recognized startups >100k.
product market fit:
Product-Market Fit (PMF) is the degree to which a product satisfies strong market demand.

Marc Andreessen's definition: 'Being in a good market with a product that can satisfy that market.'

Signs of PMF: Organic word-of-mouth, customers upset if you shut down, rapid growth.
venture capital:
Venture Capital (VC) funds early-stage, high-risk companies in exchange for equity.

Stages: Seed → Series A → Series B → Series C → IPO.

Top Indian VCs: Sequoia India (Peak XV), Nexus, Matrix Partners, Accel India.
bioinformatics:
Bioinformatics applies computational methods to analyze biological data.

Key tasks: DNA sequence analysis, protein structure prediction, genomics.

Tools: BLAST, Biopython, Galaxy, R Bioconductor.
operating system:
An OS manages hardware and provides services for software to run.

Functions: Process management, Memory management, File system, Device drivers.

Examples: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS.
linux:
Linux is the dominant open-source operating system for servers, embedded systems, and development.

Key distros: Ubuntu, Debian, CentOS, Arch, Fedora.

Essential commands: ls, cd, grep, find, chmod, ps, top, curl, wget, ssh, scp.
ollama:
Ollama lets you run large language models locally on your own machine — no internet needed.

How to use: `ollama run mistral` or `ollama run llama3`.

Popular models: TinyLlama (1.1B, fast), Mistral 7B, LLaMA 3 8B, Phi-3 Medium.

API: POST http://localhost:11434/api/generate
